name: Mykel Kochenderfer
title: Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI and Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Department of Aeronautics & Astronautics (courtesy appointment in Computer Science)
research_topics: aircraft collision avoidance and air traffic control
safety validation and failure discovery for safety-critical autonomy
autonomous vehicles and human driver behavior modeling
AI safety, LLM evaluation and red-teaming
current_direction: Autonomy for space operations: satellite ground-station siting, multi-spacecraft collision avoidance, deep-space science planning
Safety validation by actively hunting failures in deployed autonomy (importance sampling, PCA, diffusion-based failure samplers)
Runtime assurance and certifiable perception for vision-based aviation (landing systems, pose-estimation protection levels)
LLM/foundation-model safety: evaluation science, reasoning-failure signatures, red-teaming and evaluation reporting
Generative models (flow matching, diffusion) as machinery inside sequential decision making
current_direction_basis: Inferred from 2026 arXiv preprints co-authored by Kochenderfer and fetched via the arXiv API on 2026-08-31: 'Protection Levels for Vision-Based Pose Estimation' (2026-08-09), 'Semi-Decentralized Multi-Spacecraft Collision Avoidance under Communication Constraints' (2026-07-29), 'Importance Sampling and PCA for Finding Failures in Commercial Autonomous Vehicles' (2026-07-20), 'Free-Placement Optimization of Ground Station Locations for Low-Earth Orbit Satellites' (2026-06-10), 'Evaluation Cards: An Interpretive Layer for AI Evaluation Reporting' (2026-06-08), 'How Language Models Fail: Token-Level Signatures of Committed and Persistent Reasoning Failures' (2026-06-04), and 'Simplifying Flow Matching Transformations with Low-Rank Mixture Models' (2026-06-29); plus OpenAlex 2025-2026 records for the IEEE Aerospace 2026 ground-station paper, the 2025 DASC runtime-assurance paper, and the 2025 ITSC diffusion-failure-sampler paper. The space, LLM-safety and failure-search emphases are also corroborated by current student research topics on the fetched SISL People page (e.g. 'Ground station optimization', 'Language red-teaming', 'Failure prediction in language model reasoning'). NOT drawn from the biography, which still frames the work mainly as air traffic control and collision avoidance.

undergrad_signals.signal: SURF (Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship) is the supported route for non-Stanford undergraduates - but the current cycle is CLOSED
undergrad_signals.note: Upgraded to 'verified' on 2026-08-31 ONLY because this pass finally fetched the SURF program page itself, which the prior two passes never did - and what it shows is disqualifying for any 'apply now' claim. The SISL FAQ text is verbatim: 'A: We have supported external students through the SURF program in the past and will continue in the future. You send application materials to that program, not to SISL. Outside of this program, SISL does not currently have funding or capacity to support non-Stanford students. If you have a fellowship and bring your own funding, please be aware of Stanford's fees for visiting student researchers (VSRs).' Following the FAQ's SURF href redirects to https://engineering.stanford.edu/SURFBayArea (HTTP 200), which confirms the undergraduate framing literally - 'Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF) Bay Area', 'an eight-week summer research program that will bring 15 motivated undergraduate students to Stanford Engineering' - and simultaneously shows THE CYCLE IS CLOSED AND ALREADY OVER: 'Application Window December 15, 2025 - February 3, 2026 @ 11:59pm PT' and 'Program Dates June 22, 2026 - August 14, 2026'. Today is 2026-08-31, so the 2026 program concluded 17 days ago and applications shut nearly seven months ago; no 2027 cycle is posted. Eligibility further narrows it: applicants must 'Be a currently-enrolled full-time non-Stanford undergraduate student', must 'Demonstrate a committed interest in pursuing graduate study toward a PhD in an engineering field', must be 'a rising junior or non-graduating senior', and 'International applicants are not eligible for 2026 SURF Bay Area.' So this route is real and genuinely undergraduate, but it is shut right now and it is a Stanford Engineering program, not a SISL position.

state_rationale: OUTREACH - independently re-verified on 2026-08-31 by a third adversarial pass that re-fetched every page live and additionally examined five SISL pages no prior pass had opened. OPENING remains WRONG, on four grounds. (1) NOT UNDERGRADUATE-SPECIFIC. The sole present-tense recruiting sentence on https://sisl.stanford.edu/ is 'If you are a Stanford student interested in becoming involved in our research, please register your interest here.' The word 'undergraduate' appears NOWHERE on the home page, FAQ, Contact, /visit/, /research/, /internal/ or /calendar/ (grepped, zero hits); sitewide it occurs only as two People-page role labels and on the /outreach/ page. A generic 'Stanford student' invitation is an open door, not an undergraduate opening. (2) THE INTAKE FORM STILL CANNOT BE VERIFIED - and this pass proved it rather than assuming it. https://forms.gle/Hsye36eXPPa8MsDB8 now returns HTTP 200 (correcting the prior record's 'exit code 000'), but the body is ~34.9KB of pure JavaScript with no title, no metadata, no FB_PUBLIC_LOAD_DATA_ payload and zero readable text - and a deliberately bogus short link returns a byte-identical 200. A response identical to one for a non-existent form cannot support an 'apply now' recommendation. (3) THE ONE REAL UNDERGRADUATE ROUTE IS CURRENTLY CLOSED. The FAQ's SURF link was followed for the first time in this pass, to https://engineering.stanford.edu/SURFBayArea (HTTP 200): 'Application Window December 15, 2025 - February 3, 2026 @ 11:59pm PT'; 'Program Dates June 22, 2026 - August 14, 2026'. As of today the 2026 program ended 17 days ago and applications closed almost seven months ago, with no 2027 cycle posted. It also demands 'a committed interest in pursuing graduate study toward a PhD', is restricted to non-Stanford undergraduates, and excludes international applicants. (4) THE LAB'S OWN LANGUAGE NARROWS THE DOOR: 'SISL cannot take on additional participants outside of established programs'; 'Do you take high school interns? Not at this time'; 'Outside of this program, SISL does not currently have funding or capacity to support non-Stanford students'; and 'We cannot promise a spot in the lab.' The only quantified intake anywhere is doctoral ('on average between 1-3 students are admitted per year'). OUTREACH rather than WATCH is justified because the lab is unambiguously active and demonstrably does host undergraduates: the live People page lists 'Vedant Srinivas / Undergraduate / Ground station optimization' and 'Danielle Pham / Undergraduate (De Anza College) / Aircraft state estimation', Pham's headshot uploaded under /2026/06/; the newly found /outreach/ page states 'REU students in SISL have worked on projects ranging from building probabilistic driving models to visualization of dynamic target surveillance problems'; and AA228/CS238 is confirmed running this term ('Lectures will be on Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9am to 10:20am in NVIDIA auditorium starting September 22, 2026', prerequisites 'basic probability (e.g., CS109) and fluency in a high-level programming language (e.g., CS106A)'), with the FAQ recommending it to would-be lab members: 'It is also recommend to take AA228 offered in the fall quarter.' ACTION FOR A STUDENT: treat this as a warm outreach target, NOT an application. A Stanford undergraduate should submit the home-page interest form - opening it in a real browser first, since it cannot be confirmed live from here - take AA228 this fall, and attend lab meetings, which the FAQ explicitly invites. A non-Stanford undergraduate has no open route today: SURF is the lab's stated channel and its next cycle would be expected to open around mid-December, so this record should be re-checked then. No contactable email is on record - see the email fields, which remain null.
